extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students preparing for the Putnam Mathematical Competition / problem-solving practice
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation notes and worked guidance for solving Putnam-style problems across standard undergraduate topics (number theory, inequalities, sequences, calculus, differential equations, linear algebra, geometry, combinatorics, probability, etc.). Includes concise solution techniques and references to past Putnam problems for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source for Putnam problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that the questions and solutions for the Putnam examinations are published in the American Mathematical Monthly. Generally, you may find them close to the end of each volume, in the October or November issue. Back issues of the Monthly can be found in the mathematics library (SS 622).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult American Mathematical Monthly (Oct/Nov issues) and math library back issues (SS 622) to collect past Putnam problems and solutions for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize study by topic areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Putnam problems are grouped by topics (Number Theory, Real Numbers, Inequalities, Sequences/Series/Recurrences, Calculus/Analysis, Differential Equations, Geometry, Group Theory and Axiomatics, Fields, Algebra, Matrices/Determinants/Linear Algebra, Combinatorics, Probability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the topical organization to focus practice and review the standard theorems/methods associated with each area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence: geometric first-order
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = a xn has the general solution xn = x1 a^{n−1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize simple multiplicative recurrences as geometric progressions; apply directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence: arithmetic first-order
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = xn + b has the general solution xn = x1 + (n − 1)b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize simple additive recurrences as arithmetic progressions; apply directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear nonhomogeneous first-order via constant shift
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = a xn + b (with a ≠ 1) can be rewritten xn+1 + k = a(xn + k) where (a − 1)k = b and so reduces to the geometric recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve by finding fixed point k = b/(a−1), shift variables and reduce to homogeneous case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-order linear recurrence: distinct roots case
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = a xn + b xn−1; if a^2 − 4b ≠ 0 and the distinct roots of the characteristic polynomial are r1 and r2, then the general solution is xn = c1 r1^n + c2 r2^n with constants determined by initial conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute characteristic polynomial t^2 − a t − b, find roots, and form linear combination of root powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-order linear recurrence: repeated root case
rubrics_metrics.description: If a^2 − 4b = 0 and r is the double root, then xn = (c1 n + c0) r^n with c1, c0 chosen from initial conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characteristic polynomial has repeated root, multiply exponential term by polynomial in n of degree (multiplicity−1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce certain three-term recurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = (1 − s) xn + s xn−1 + r can be rewritten xn+1 − xn = −s(xn − xn−1) + r and solved by previously given methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert to a recurrence for the differences and apply linear methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift trick for three-term nonhomogeneous recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: xn+1 = a xn + b xn−1 + c where a + b ≠ 1 can be rewritten (xn+1 + k) = a(xn + k) + b(xn−1 + k) where (a + b − 1)k = c and solved for xn + k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose k to eliminate the constant term, reducing to homogeneous recurrence in shifted sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: General homogeneous linear recursion and characteristic polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: General homogeneous linear recursion: xn+k = a_{k−1} xn+k−1 + · · · + a0 xn. Characteristic polynomial is t^k − a_{k−1} t^{k−1} − · · · − a0. If r is a root of multiplicity m then solution contains terms (c_{m−1} n^{m−1} + · · · + c0) r^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve by factoring characteristic polynomial; multiplicities produce polynomial factors in n multiplying r^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-order linear ODE: integrating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear y' + p(x) y = q(x). Multiply through by the integrating factor exp(∫ p(x) dx) to obtain (y exp(∫ p(x) dx))' = q(x) exp(∫ p(x) dx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrating factor to reduce to exact derivative and integrate; standard method for first-order linear ODEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of variables
rubrics_metrics.description: y' = f(x) g(y). Put in the form dy/g(y) = f(x) dx and integrate both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when right-hand side factors into function of x times function of y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneous first-order ODE via substitution y = u x
rubrics_metrics.description: y' = f(x, y) where f(tx, ty) = f(x, y). Let y = u x, y' = u' x + u to reduce to u' x + u = f(1, u).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homogeneity property to reduce to equation in u(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractional-linear first-order ODEs (ratio of linear forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: y' = (a x + b y)/(c x + d y). Solve as in the homogeneous substitution case or introduce auxiliary variable t and convert to system dy/dt = a x + b y, dx/dt = c x + d y and attempt exponential solutions; if repeated eigenvalue, use polynomial-times-exponential ansatz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert to linear system or use substitution to reduce to standard forms; try solutions of exponential type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified fractional-linear ODE with constants: two-case reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: y' = (ax + by + c)/(hx + ky + r). (i) If ak − bh ≠ 0, choose p, q so that ap + bq + c = 0 and hp + kq + r = 0 and change variables X = x − p, Y = y − q. (ii) If ak − bh = 0, set u = ax + by + c to obtain a separable equation in y and u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate coordinates to remove constants when possible; otherwise find invariant linear combination to separate variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact equation criterion and solution construction
rubrics_metrics.description: General linear exact equation P(x, y) dx + Q(x, y) dy = 0. Define Δ ≡ ∂P/∂y − ∂Q/∂x. If Δ = 0 the equation has solution f(x,y)=C where ∂f/∂x = P and ∂f/∂y = Q, and explicit integrals are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check exactness (Δ=0) and integrate P wrt x and Q wrt y, matching arbitrary functions to construct potential function f(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inexact equation: find integrating factor heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: For P dx + Q dy = 0 with Δ ≠ 0 one seeks an integrating factor h(x,y) satisfying h(Δ) + P ∂h/∂y − Q ∂h/∂x = 0. Try assuming h depends on x alone, y alone, xy, x/y or y/x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no general method; attempt simple ansatz for h (function of x only, y only, product or ratio) to make equation exact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riccati equation reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Riccati y' = f0(x) + f1(x) y + f2(x) y^2 where f2(x) ≠ 0. If a particular solution y0 is known, set y = y0 + 1/u to reduce the equation to a linear first-order ODE in u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding one particular solution linearizes the Riccati via the substitution y = y0 + 1/u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bernoulli equation substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Bernoulli y' + p(x) y = q(x) y^n. If n = 0 or 1 treat as linear or separable; if n ≠ 0,1 set u = y^{1−n} to obtain a linear first-order equation in u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard substitution transforms Bernoulli to linear equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear nth-order constant-coefficient ODE: complementary + particular
rubrics_metrics.description: A linear nth-order ODE with constant coefficients has general solution equal to the complementary function (general solution of homogeneous equation) plus a particular integral (any solution of the inhomogeneous equation). The complementary function is built from roots of auxiliary polynomial: multiplicity r of root λ yields terms (polynomial of degree r−1)×e^{λ x}. A particular integral can be found when q(x) is sum of terms h(x) e^{ρ x} by the method of annihilators/undetermined coefficients or operational calculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find characteristic polynomial roots for complementary solution; for particular solution try an ansatz matching form of q(x) multiplied by polynomial factor if ρ is root of characteristic polynomial. Use complex exponentials for sine/cosine forcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational calculus rules for ODE operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D denote differentiation. For polynomial p(t) we have p(D) e^{r x} = p(r) e^{r x} and p(D)(u e^{r x}) = e^{r x} p(D + r) u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use operator substitution to bring exponential factor through differential operator and reduce to differential equations for u; this helps find particular integrals without many undetermined coefficients cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example method: complexification and choice of u
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a particular integral, take complex forcing e^{(α+iβ)x}, seek solution y = u e^{(α+iβ)x}, bring exponential through operator, obtain differential equations for u and choose u with low-degree derivatives (e.g., set higher derivatives to 0) to satisfy the chain of equations. Take imaginary part if original forcing was sin/cos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated with worked examples where one picks u so that higher derivatives vanish and solves for remaining derivatives; practical technique to avoid many special-cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group theory: review core concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: The following concepts should be reviewed: group, order of groups and elements, cyclic group, conjugate elements, commute, homomorphism, isomorphism, subgroup, factor group, right and left cosets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solid understanding of these definitions and examples is essential for solving Putnam group-theory problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lagrange's Theorem (study required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lagrange’s Theorem: The order of a finite group is exactly divisible by the order of any subgroup and by the order of any element of the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use order divisibility constraints frequently in group-theoretic problem solving; memorize and apply consequences (e.g., Sylow-style arguments in competition problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences: prime-order groups and generators
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of prime order is necessarily commutative and has no proper subgroups. A subset S of a group G is a set of generators for G iff every element of G can be written as a product of elements in S and their inverses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when order arguments force a group to be cyclic/abelian and when a small generating set suffices; these are common Putnam lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix function via power series (example: sin A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any square matrix A, define sin A by the usual power series sin A = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (−1)^n/(2n+1)! A^{2n+1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrix functions can be defined via convergent power series; use spectral decomposition or series manipulation to reason about values (e.g., whether sin A equals a given matrix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use classic Putnam problem practice (illustrative lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: The document lists numerous past Putnam problems (by year and problem number) across topics as recommended practice problems, e.g., 1998-A-4, 1997-B-3, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through the listed past problems in each topical section to internalize techniques; use problem lists as a syllabus for targeted practice.
